problem: Prior VLN agents (Speaker-Follower, RCM, Self-Monitoring, EnvDrop) are trained only on action supervision plus cross-modal grounding. They ignore semantic signals already present in the environment and trajectory: what past actions mean, how far along the path the agent is, the geometry of the navigation graph and the next heading, and whether the trajectory matches the instruction. The one existing progress signal (Self-Monitoring's normalized-distance progress monitor) uses biased, noisy labels.
motivation: Self-supervised auxiliary tasks improve data efficiency, robustness and domain adaptation in RL and vision (e.g. UNREAL-style losses, test-time training). The seen/unseen domain gap is the main failure of VLN agents. Reasoning heads also make the agent's behaviour interpretable, and the auxiliary losses can still be applied when fine-tuning on unseen environments (pre-exploration) to align representations across domains.
key_idea: Attach four self-supervised reasoning heads to an EnvDrop-style VLN agent and train them jointly with the navigation IL+RL objective. The heads are trajectory retelling (end-to-end speaker), step-based progress estimation, next-angle prediction, and instruction–trajectory matching.
insight: The four auxiliary tasks each add a small amount and are complementary. Measured as unseen SPL over a 42.89 baseline: +Speaker 45.24, +Progress 44.74, +Matching 44.10, +Angle 43.77, all four together 45.67. They are strongly synergistic with back-translation augmentation: BT alone reaches 46.84, BT plus the aux losses reaches 50.29, and the gain is larger than the sum of the individual gains, as the aux signals help regularize noisy augmented data. Label design matters for progress estimation. Step-percentage labels with BCE (44.74 unseen SPL, error 0.16) beat step labels with MSE (43.16) and the distance-based Progress Monitor (42.21, below the baseline), showing that distance-based progress labels are noisy. For retelling, an end-to-end teacher-forced speaker loss beats using the speaker as an RL reward (Matching Critic, 43.44) or student forcing (43.78). A speaker that shares the navigation language context reaches higher word accuracy (38.49 vs 25.95) but lower SPL, i.e. it overfits the auxiliary task.
method: Vision-language encoder: 36 panoramic view features plus orientation (sin/cos of heading and elevation) are attended using the previous cross-modal context and fed to a trajectory-level LSTM_v, giving a vision history context. A Bi-LSTM encodes the instruction (its mean pool gives a global language context), and word features are attended with the vision context to produce the cross-modal context f̂_t.

Action prediction and navigation objectives: attention/softmax over candidate features (k graph neighbours + stop) in the panoramic action space. The IL loss (teacher forcing) and the A2C RL loss (student forcing, same instruction) have their gradients summed per update.

Trajectory retelling task: an end-to-end speaker. LSTM_s runs teacher-forced over the instruction word embeddings, each step attends over the trajectory's vision history contexts, and the model is trained with word-level cross-entropy. Applied only in IL.
Progress estimation task: predicts step-percentage progress t/T as a soft label {t/T, 1−t/T} via BCE on sigmoid(W_r f̂_t), replacing the normalized-distance MSE labels of the Self-Monitoring agent.

Cross-modal matching task: the global language context is shuffled with other samples in the batch with p=0.5, concatenated with f̂_t, and a binary classifier predicts whether trajectory and instruction match.
Angle prediction task: regression from f̂_t to the teacher action's orientation. Applied only in IL.

Training schedule: all aux losses summed with weight 1, 80K iterations per stage. Stage 1 trains on R2R train. Stage 2 fine-tunes on speaker back-translation data from training environments (EnvDrop). Stage 3 fine-tunes on speaker-augmented data sampled from test environments (pre-explore). Aux weights are halved on augmented data.

setting.backbone: LSTM/Bi-LSTM attention seq2seq agent built on Environmental Dropout (EnvDrop). Precomputed image features, whose CNN is not specified in the paper (EnvDrop uses ImageNet ResNet-152). Trained from scratch.
setting.training_data: R2R train (61 environments, 14,025 instructions). Speaker back-translation augmented data sampled from training environments (EnvDrop-style). For the pre-explore setting, additional speaker-augmented paths sampled from the test/unseen environments.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views, precomputed CNN features) + view orientation features
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space: neighbour nodes + stop)
setting.privileged: none for Single Run. The Pre-explore setting fine-tunes on unseen/test environments (pre-exploration). The Beam Search setting uses beam search over trajectories.

numbers_note: Test-set leaderboard numbers are printed as fractions with two decimals (e.g. 0.55); they are converted to percent here. Validation numbers come from ablation tables and use the percent format. Val numbers for the pre-explore model are not reported. OR in the paper is oracle success, mapped to OSR here.
results: On the R2R test (unseen) leaderboard, AuxRN reaches SPL 51 / SR 55 in the single-run setting and SPL 65 / SR 68 / NE 3.69 with pre-exploration. The previous state of the art, Environmental Dropout, had 47 / 51 and 61 / 64 in the same settings. With beam search AuxRN reaches SR 71 vs EnvDrop's 69, with a trajectory length of only 41 m vs 687. On val-unseen, the auxiliary losses raise the EnvDrop baseline SPL from 42.89 to 45.67 without augmentation, and from 46.84 to 50.29 with back-translation.
limitations: Evaluated only on R2R in the discrete nav-graph setting. The headline 65% SPL relies on pre-exploration fine-tuning in the test environments.

Gains from individual auxiliary tasks are small (about 1–2 SPL), with no variance or seed reporting. The matching task alone hurts val-seen SPL (53.55 vs 55.87). Loss weights are fixed heuristically (1, halved on augmented data).
Retelling and angle losses need teacher trajectories, so they apply only during IL, not RL. Beam-search SPL remains low (21).
